text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - South Korea bought 87,500 tonnes of Chinese corn for September arrival. Of that, 30,000 was purchased from Louis Dreyfus and 57,500 tonnes from Cargill Inc. Prices ranged from $140.90 to $143.35 per tonne.

WHEAT SALE - Taiwan bought 26,000 tonnes U.S. wheat for May 5-25 arrival. It bought 16,000 tonnes dark northern spring wheat for $198.20 per tonne, 6,900 tonnes hard red winter for $189.39 per tonne and 3,100 tonnes white wheat for $168.13 per tonne.
WHEAT SALES - France sold 3,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Iraq in a food aid tender for April 8-30 shipment. The price was 1,029.60 francs per tonne, FOB Caen, via the Rome-based World Food Programme.

- Syria sold 18,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat to Cargill International for $195.50 per tonne FOB. Syria also sold 50,000 tonnes durum wheat to a Cypriot firm for $195 per tonne for April/May shipment.
WHEAT TENDER - Iraq is still negotiating for 50,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat and a reply is expected this week.
WHEAT TENDER - Cyprus cancelled a combined 18,000-tonne wheat tender. It gave no reason for the cancellation. The tender was for 10,000 tonnes spring wheat and 8,000 tonnes durum.
- South Korea seeks 23,000 tonnes U.S. No.1 wheat. Offers were due by 1400 local/0500 GMT Friday. Shipment was set for May 5-June 5 shipment.
VEGOIL TENDER - Egypt seeks up to 45,000 tonnes of vegetable oils for May delivery. The deadline for bids was April 2.
BARLEY TENDER - The South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.
RICE TENDER - Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.

MARKET TALK - China has not offered much corn on the market recently and may not do so until the middle of the year, traders in China and Hong Kong said. Traders said several glitches had hurt exports, including railway logjams that were interrupting the flow of corn toward ports. They said export licenses were also hard to come by. But none said China planned to reissue a ban on corn exports....India's Civil Supplies Ministry said foodgrain stocks were at 20.36 million tonnes as of December 1, 1996, down sharply from 29.89 million the previous year....The Australian Wheat Board declined to comment on rumored wheat sales to India....The United States said on Thursday it would consider providing additional food aid to North Korea on humanitarian grounds but declined to tie aid directly to a deal for Korean peninsula peace talks.
